The Critical Text of Q

Copyright (c) 1996 by the International Q Project. No reprinting without
written permission!

This is the English translation of the text of Q as it has been
reconstructed by the International Q Project of the Society of
Biblical Literature, as of November 1996. More changes are yet
to come. Please do not redistribute this text; an official version
is in the works.

- Sterling Bjorndahl

Sigla
:

[ ]    These surround reconstructed text that a probable of only {C} on a
       descending scale of {A} to {D}. The absence of space between empty
       brackets, i.e. [], indicates with a probability of {C} that no text is
       assumed to have been present there, despite the existence of some text
       in Matthew and/or Luke at that point. Most text in Q is rated at a
       probability of {A} or {B}.

...    Some text is assumed to have existed in Q at this location, but its
       exact wording cannot be reconstructed. If printed between brackets, 
       [...], it is presumed only with a {C} grade that something was there.

..     Two dots indicate that there is a possibility of grade {D} that there
       was text there, or that it is undecided whether there was any text
       there.

< >    The text thus enclosed is a conjectural emendation, found as such in
       neither Matthew nor Luke.

<< >>  In the English translation of Q, these surround a text where the exact
       words could not be reconstructed but where the gist or train of thought
       is clear. They also surround verses that are not reconstructable but
       which are determined to probably be in Q nevertheless - particularly in
       those few cases where a text is considered to be part of Q despite its
       existence in only one of Matthew or Luke.

Note: The chapter and verse references are according to Luke's Gospel, so
that e.g. Q 3:7-9 refers to Luke 3:7-9 and its parallel in Matthew (3:7-10).
A Synopsis of the Gospels, or John Kloppenborg's 
Q Parallels
,
can help the reader identify the Matthean parallels.
